title: lavatera olbia subsp. hispida
intro: Lavatera olbia subsp. hispida, commonly known as the Mexican tree mallow, is a plant species in the Malvaceae family, native to Mexico and the southwestern United States. This plant is known for its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which may help to soothe wounds, reduce fever, and prevent infections. The therapeutic actions of Lavatera olbia subsp. hispida include its ability to act as an antiseptic, astringent, and demulcent, making it useful for treating skin conditions and respiratory issues. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
